expected_level_description: You can: - apply the approach to real problems and consider all relevant information - apply appropriate rigour to ensure a full solution is designed and achieves the business outcome

You can: - demonstrate a deep understanding of security concepts and can apply them to a technical level - effectively translate and accurately communicate security and risk implications to technical and non-technical stakeholders - successfully respond to challenges - manage stakeholder expectations and be flexible, adapting to stakeholder reactions to reach consensus
You can: - design and review system architectures through the application of patterns and principles

You can: - work with risk owners to advise and give feedback - advise on risk impact and whether it's within risk tolerance - describe different risk methodologies and how these are applied, as well as the proportionality of risk
You can: - advise on developments to security properties in technology - identify new technologies and design their use in a business context
You can: - explain the effect of vulnerabilities on current and future designs - share information on a range of systems, but may specialise in one
You can: - interpret and apply an understanding of policy and process, business architecture, and legal and political implications to assist the development of technical solutions or controls

You can: - explain the clinical and care workflows your work supports - use common health care terms correctly with clinical and care colleagues - recognise when a change could affect patient care and raise it

You can: - lead data protection impact assessments and information sharing agreements - advise teams on lawful basis, consent, confidentiality, and retention - investigate incidents and recommend improvements
You can: - design and run identity and access services - review access regularly and fix problems
You can: - prioritise vulnerabilities by risk, including to patient services - scope and manage penetration tests and remediation
You can: - take part in hazard workshops and contribute to a hazard log - follow the clinical risk management process for your work - provide evidence for a clinical safety case, such as test results
You can: - explain that some health software is regulated as a medical device - know who to ask when a product might be a medical device
